drivers.name: 20% off promotion (featured in ad)
drivers.evidence: Noise-adjusted past promotion uplift: x1.43 (13 events). Most recent 20% off (2025-12-08) lifted only x1.11. Deeper discount than prior 15% or 10% events, but no prior 20% off on a non-holiday week showed strong lift. No evidence of overreaction or stockpiling.

adjustment.analysis: The 20% off promotion is featured in the weekly ad and matches a past 20% off event (2025-12-08) that lifted sales by x1.11. However, that was a non-holiday week with a smaller lift than other promotions. The noise-adjusted uplift from 13 past promotions is x1.43, but the most recent one (2025-12-08) was weak, suggesting limited carryover. The current price drop is deeper than past 15% or 10% discounts, but no prior 20% off on a non-holiday week shows strong lift. The Memorial Day week (x2.37) had a holiday, so not directly comparable. No evidence of pantry-loading risk. The classical model’s x1.43 is reasonable but overconfident given sparse high-impact data. Shrink toward baseline. The baseline already reflects a 37% trend and seasonal ramp.

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-33% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
